The United States never received immigration exceeding 11 per cent of the population, while according to the figures of the Department of the Interior in Canada, from 1901 to 1911, Canada will receive foreign-born immigrants to the extent of 37 per cent of the population. When the United States had fifty million of a population they did not receive more than 300,000 immigrants per year. President Roosevelt and the scientists and economists of that country arc alarmed and are doing what they can to exclude immigrants. I could quote more figures to show the House that since 1850 in tue United States the foreign-born population was never more than 15 per cent of the total population. In Canada the foreign-born population is 12-7 per cent of the total population. The total population of Canada was at the last census, I believe, 5,371,315, and the foreign-born population is a little more than 684,000. In four years, according to the estimate of the Department of the Interior, the total population of Canada will probably be about eight million and the foreign-born population will be about two and a half million; that is 30 per cent of foreign-born population. But, as to this assimilation, let us hear a voice from the west; let us hear a man who ought to know something about assimilation of population in the Northwest, and here is what was said by Mr. Roblin, Premier of Manitoba, speaking at Pictou on June the 10th, 1907:
To show that I am not mistaken in my conclusions upon this point, allow me to point out this fact-that in the last ten years, according to the figures compiled by the Immigra-gration Department of the Dominion, there have come into Canada, in round figures,
900,000	souls. Of these, only 350,000 were British born, the balance (550,000) are either Americans-citizens of the United States to the South of us-or people from continental Europe. I may say that, according to the same authority, a larger proportion of those who came to us who were not British born, covering this period, came from the United States, than came from Europe.
Now, it is only a logical conclusion to say that the same ratio at least will be maintained in the future as has obtained in the

past. It is a reasonable statement, therefore, to say that a country of eighty millions of people immediately adjoining, who have no more free lands to offer to their people, will naturally, by virtue of the natural increase of population, continue in much larger percentage to emigrate to our ' last west,' as it is called. The same with continental Europe. They have 400,000,000 of people to draw from, and they are coming from every nation, while we have only about 40,000,000 to draw from in so far as the United Kingdom is concerned.
Foreigners will control.
Without any doubt whatever, it is only a matter of five, certainly not more than ten, years with the same ratio of immigration that has characterized the last five years, when the foreign-born citizens of western Canada can, if they choose, take all matters of government absolutely into their own hands.
That speech was published in the press all over the Dominion ; it was read by the people of the west and I am told that the popularity of the Premier of Manitoba has not suffered thereby. Even the Minister of the Interior himself speaking of the North Atlantic Trading Company said that this system of paying bonuses to individual booking agents cannot be checked. More than that, we have in the old country, hypnotized immigrants to come to Canada and I do not want any better proof of that than the statement of Mr. Bruce Walker contained at page G6 of the report of the Department of the Interior for 1907, where he says :
Since I have been in charge of the propaganda here, under your Lordship, I have sought to impose a higher standard upon those classes of emigrants over which we have control particularly, and over all emigrants generally. I disapprove strongly of efforts to paint Canada as a ' land flowing with milk and honey/ or a place providing an easy existence for those who readily tired of work. The greatest attraction of our country is the ready results that follow energy, ambition and determination.
Here, according to the report of an officer of the department, Canada has been represented as a land flowing with milk and honey. We have been told by the Minister of the Interior that we do not pay bonuses for immigrants to come to this country, and that the bonus to the booking agent is simply for advertising Canada. Does the minister pretend that the advertising of Canada in the old country is read only by farm labourers or railway navvies and those of the classes we desire to bring here ? Does he not know that the advertising of Canada reaches every class of the population there and that it brings to our country the disabled and degenerate. Such representation have even a more decided effect on a population of destitutes. I say that the immigration agents have brought immigrants to this country under false pretenses and I further say that when the government paid these bonuses they had no proof that they were paid on account of farm la-Mr. A. LAVERGNE.
bourers or navvies, or those whom the regulations prescribed it should be paid on. I want no better evidence of that than that which is given by Mr. Scott, superintendent of immigration, before the Committee on Colonization and Agriculture, and which I quote :
By Dr. Sproule:
Q. As I understand it you merely ask immigrants whether they contemplate following agricultural pursuits when they come here? -A. We do at the ocean ports.
Q. That is all the information you have as to the classes to which they belong?-A. Yes, they are questioned as to their age and occupation.
Q. What occupation they have been following?-A. What occupation they have been following in the old country and the manifest is prepared by the purser of the ship who is not a government officer and certified to by the master of the vessel.
Therefore, the certificate of the occupation of the man who comes to this country is prepared by the very people who have an interest in bringing him here and receiving the bonus, as is proven by the evidence of an officer of the department. I quote further from the evidence of Mr. Scott :
I should have thought a government officer would look after that work and see that nobody but certain classes were sent out?-A. Anybody who has the money can buy a ticket.
Q. But if he has the money will he get the bonus?-A. No, but I say any one can buy a ticket in the old country.
Q. The reason I ask is because I know of several men who came out here; I was told they were farm labourers and had come out to follow farming and I took the trouble to inquire and in the case of six or seven there was not a single man who was on a farm in his life?-A. That might be quite true.
Here is the superintendent of immigration saying that bonuses might be paid on men who were brought out as farm labourers and who never had worked on a farm in their lives. The examination of Mr. Scott continued :
Q. And yet they were sent out and called farm hands?-A. No, not called farpi hands. They were sent out here to follow agricultural pursuits and on an English farm the labourer receives as good money as he' receives here and in addition he gets work all the year round instead of only seven or eight months.
if. Tt seems to me that is not the question; it is whether we were misled or not in reference to the class of people coming out?-A. I do not think so. The manifest shows the evidence.
Q. What manifest?-A. The manifest signed by the purser of the ship.
Q. Do you not pay the booking agent?-A. Only if they are agriculturists or intend to follow that occupation in this country.
Therefore a man can buy his ticket from a booking agent and the booking agent does not care about Canada, he cares only, about

the bonus he is going to get and the commission on the ticket and he says to the man: Just say that you are a farm labourer or that you want to work on a railway and you will get into Canada. The examination of Mr. Scott continued:
By Mr. Wilson:
Q. If they say they intend it ?-A. Yes.
By Mr. Ross:
Q. Do I understand they make a declaration to that effect?-A. They answer questions at the port.
Q With reference to the Salvation Army do you insist upon the same class that you pay the bonus on?-A. The same class.
Q. Or do you pay the bonus on all they bring f-A. No, on the same class.
Q. What was the percentage they bring?- A. I think possibly their percentage has been a little higher than some of the others.
I want the House to remember well what has been said about the Salvation Army because when we come to consider the ports [DOT]of Canada we will see the acts of the Salvation Army.
Q. Has the arrangement been completed with reference to the land they get in the Northwest?-A. I know nothing about the land.
Q. Will that not come under your office to some extent?-A. No, we have nothing to dro with the land in the west.
Q. You have nothing to do with where they shall be sent?-A. No.
Q. Who does that?-A. The land branch, I suppose.
Here is the Superintendent of Immigration who does not know' where the immigrant goes in this country.

maintopic: SUPPLY-STATUTES OF THE PROVINCE OF SASKATCHEWAN.
speechtext:
Hear, hear.
Mr. ARMAND LA VEItG-NE. But we are told by the Minister of the Interior that the bonus is paid on the immigrant, not to the Immigrant. As I have said we have been advertising Canada as a patent medicine Is advertised and what has been the result ? The result has been, as with any patent medicine, that the diseased have been coming to this country. I care not what kind of disease they are suffering from, mental, physical or moral, it is certain that they have been coming to Canada. As the minister himself said when he was a plain member of this House, the best advertisement we can have for this country is a contented settler and as the minister has proven to-night by trying to show that we do not pay a bonus on the greater part of the immigrants we receive. Stopping the bonus will not stop immigration coming to this country but we will have the quality instead of having the quantity sent to us by different booking agents to secure the bonus paid by our country. To-night, as last year when the immigration question was threshed out in this House, the minister tried to prove that we were not paying bonuses on many of these immigrants sent out by organizations but later when the subsidies came down it
was seen that the immigration agents of the government, such as the Church Army, were asking in England for such immigrants as these, tramps, loafers, ex-convicts, drunkards hooligans. That is the kind of immigration we have been receiving in this country, and these immigrants have been canvassed by the very agents of this government. Has this government disallowed the Church Army? I have searched in every record of the government, in every record of the Department of the Interior, and I have not seen that the Church Army has been disallowed, except that this year a certain number of their immigrants were sent back. Why ? Because last year we denounced this policy of the government and were called little Canadians by that broad, that immense Canadian, the present Minister of the Interior.
The Salvation Army is still an immigration agent of this department and what have we seen in Quebec? I have no hesitation in saying and I dare the minister to contradict me, that nine-tenths of the immigration which has been sent out by the Salvation Army is bad, and I want no other evidence than that of the doctors who receive the immigrants at the port of Quebec. And I say this too, that there has been some collusion between the Salvation Army and the officers at Quebec.

speakerposition: Minister of the Interior; Superintendent-General of Indian Affairs
maintopic: SUPPLY-STATUTES OF THE PROVINCE OF SASKATCHEWAN.
speechtext: My hon. friend has asked me to deny a statement he has made and I do not want his statement to go on record without my denial.

maintopic: SUPPLY-STATUTES OF THE PROVINCE OF SASKATCHEWAN.
speechtext: Then I defy the minister to have an inquiry into the Salvation Army and the immigrants it has brought into Quebec, and to ask the doctors at Quebec to give their evidence; but I hope this time the government will not stop the mouths of the witnesses who give evidence. There has been collusion between the officers at Quebec and the Salvation Army, and I have it from the very officers who receive the immigrants at Quebec that before they pass the medical examination of the officers of his department the immigrants of the Salvation Army go to the barracks and get the password of the Salvation Army at Quebec and then go back and answer the doctor. The minister cannot contradict that if he looks at the correspondence produced.

speakerposition: Minister of the Interior; Superintendent-General of Indian Affairs
maintopic: SUPPLY-STATUTES OF THE PROVINCE OF SASKATCHEWAN.
speechtext: The hon. member is making a great many statements which he puts forward as statements of fact. The statement he has made just now that members of the Salvation Army or immigrants coming out under the auspices of the Salvation Army are treated any differently from any other immigrants who come out, so far as my knowledge goes, is absolutely incorrect; and if I can by any means demonstrate that it is the fact we will have a change in the immigration service at Quebec immediately.

maintopic: SUPPLY-STATUTES OF THE PROVINCE OF SASKATCHEWAN.
speechtext: I accept the personal denial of the minister but you will notice that it is not an official denial and I repeat it officially

speakerposition: Minister of the Interior; Superintendent-General of Indian Affairs
maintopic: SUPPLY-STATUTES OF THE PROVINCE OF SASKATCHEWAN.
speechtext: We will make this as official as we can. If my hon. friend will give me name, place and date, I will make it official inside of twenty-four hours.

maintopic: SUPPLY-STATUTES OF THE PROVINCE OF SASKATCHEWAN.
speechtext: All last summer, the immigrants brought out by the Salvation Army were sent to the barracks and there they got the password from the Salvation Army officers to answer the doctors of the Immigration Department. Not only that but a report was made to the Interior Department here and after that report was made, it was understood by Mr. Doyle and the immigration doctors at Quebec, I think Dr. Nadeau and Dr. Potvin, that if there were one hundred Salvation Army immigrants they would pass before the doctor first but if less they would go to the barracks first. That is the statement I have to make and on it I would like the department to throw more light.

speakerposition: Minister of the Interior; Superintendent-General of Indian Affairs
maintopic: SUPPLY-STATUTES OF THE PROVINCE OF SASKATCHEWAN.
speechtext: I will guarantee all the light that is possible and if the statement is true I will consider myself under very serious obligations to my hon. friend for making it.

maintopic: SUPPLY-STATUTES OF THE PROVINCE OF SASKATCHEWAN.
speechtext:
I knew the minister would be under obligations. Last year we made statements and he made changes, and this year he will make more. If he will have an investigation of the methods at Quebec he will learn many things that will enlighten him and he will be still more grateful to me.
But the minister has told us that if the immigrant was not satisfactory he would be deported. If he came here in transit through Canada to the United States he would be deported, and was generally deported, and no immigrant who was brought into this country and was found undesirable was not deported. Let us look at the statement. First of all we see no report of the immigrants refused by the United States who have been deported by this government and more than that we see that the very immigrants coming to this country who should have been deported have not always been deported. We have had to-night the first declaration of the minister on this subject. We see certainly that some have been deported at the port of entry for certain reasons, but there are some in Montreal who come under section 33 of the Immigration Act who have not been deported. The minister says that no complaint has been made.
I understand that quite well. Suppose a city like Montreal or Toronto would make a complaint, do you know what the minister would answer? Yes, they will be deported, but you pay the cost. That is the regulation of the Immigration Department. I say that with the number of immigrants coming

speakerposition: Minister of the Interior; Superintendent-General of Indian Affairs
maintopic: SUPPLY-STATUTES OF THE PROVINCE OF SASKATCHEWAN.
speechtext: to this country it would be impossible for a city to do this, it would ruin the budget of any city to have to deport the immigrants received who are not desirable.

speakerposition: Minister of the Interior; Superintendent-General of Indian Affairs
maintopic: SUPPLY-STATUTES OF THE PROVINCE OF SASKATCHEWAN.
speechtext: It may be that my hon. friend is not anxious to adhere strictly to the facts but he should get a little closer to them. The Act says that the immigrant is to be deported at the cost of the transportation company bringing him.

maintopic: SUPPLY-STATUTES OF THE PROVINCE OF SASKATCHEWAN.
speechtext: Or those making the complaint.

speakerposition: Minister of the Interior; Superintendent-General of Indian Affairs
maintopic: SUPPLY-STATUTES OF THE PROVINCE OF SASKATCHEWAN.
speechtext: No.

maintopic: SUPPLY-STATUTES OF THE PROVINCE OF SASKATCHEWAN.
speechtext: I asked the minister and he said yes.

speakerposition: Minister of the Interior; Superintendent-General of Indian Affairs
maintopic: SUPPLY-STATUTES OF THE PROVINCE OF SASKATCHEWAN.
speechtext: If the transportation company is not known then at the cost of the person making the complaint.

maintopic: SUPPLY-STATUTES OF THE PROVINCE OF SASKATCHEWAN.
speechtext: Have we not seen that the transportation company is not known? We have seen from the evidence of Mr. Scott that they do not know the immigrants or where they are, and how would it be possible to know what transportation company brought them? Therefore, you would fall back on a city like Montreal or Toronto. And what do we see in those cities in the provinces of Quebec and Ontario which have received those immigrants? We see that criminality there has increased to such an extent that the public press of this country deem it advisable to publish articles on its alarming increase. Let the Minister of the Interior (Mr. Oliver) ask any judge of the assizes in Montreal or any other city, or any police magistrate, if nine-tenths of those who are convicted before them are not foreigners brought to this country at so much per head, or, if no bonus was paid on them, brought by the false pretenses of immigration agents who paint Canada as a land of promise with a view of getting the bonus on a certain number. And because of these glowing descriptions, you will always find that a good many of the abandoned and destitute in the old world will be tempted to seek better fortune in the new. There is something else. In Montreal already we have had to face the social question which until to-day was there practically unknown. Last year we had a socialistic parade and we are to have another this year. I knew the Minister of the Interior was a Liberal, but I could not know, he was a Liberal to such an extent that he wanted the red flag raised in the city of Montreal.

maintopic: SUPPLY-STATUTES OF THE PROVINCE OF SASKATCHEWAN.
speechtext: My hon. friend states that last year there was an anarchists parade ; I may say that three-fourths of those people were from New York, and were visiting in Montreal for the occasion. One or two women were among the paraders. The demonstration was stopped by the civic authorities and it will be stopped again this year.

maintopic: SUPPLY-STATUTES OF THE PROVINCE OF SASKATCHEWAN.
speechtext: My hon. friend (Mr. Mederie Martin) says that last year the parade was stopped and will be stopped again this year and that most of those who took part in it came from the United States. But if the l*on. gentlemen on this side of the House are true Liberals, it seems to me that, having brought out those immigrants under false pretenses, the least they could do, if they have brought out socialists, is to let them parade. You must respect the opinion of the immigrants who enter this country. And I must say also- even if I have to contradict my hon. friend from St. Marys (Mr. Mederie Martin) for whom I have the greatest respect-that while the parade may have been composed to a certain extent of a certain foreign element. it was composed mainly of a foreign population brought to this country through the immigration policy of the government. Is it not true that in Toronto last winter there were about 15,000 people without work and that 500 poor little children of immigrants died of starvation in that city? If that be the result of the bonus which the government pays, are we not justified in denouncing it? And if the Minister of the Interior will go to Vancouver, he will find there racial riots, which though they may not be the result of bonused immigration, are the result of throwing the door open to all kinds of immigrants. There is this exception, namely, the government put a head tax on the Chinese. But they do not put it on the Japanese. I would like the Minister of the Interior to explain the difference, from a racial or national point of view, between the Chinese and the Japanese. If there is a yellow peril, it is just as yellow with the Japanese as with the Chinese. There is this difference between the two that you will not find the Chinese despising every other nation as do the Japanese and the immigration regulations passed by the department are not above the Japanese treaty.

maintopic: SUPPLY-STATUTES OF THE PROVINCE OF SASKATCHEWAN.
speechtext: Would you keep a man out of this country because he declares himself a socialist ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-STATUTES OF THE PROVINCE OF SASKATCHEWAN.
speechtext: Certainly not, but what I say is that the socialistic movement is found among the destitute of the old world and previous to these destitutes coming out here we had not any socialists in this country.

maintopic: SUPPLY-STATUTES OF THE PROVINCE OF SASKATCHEWAN.
speechtext: Perfect nonsense.

maintopic: SUPPLY-STATUTES OF THE PROVINCE OF SASKATCHEWAN.
speechtext:
That is very easy to say, but if you go to the old country you will find two classes of people fighting against organized society and these are the socialists and one degree further down the anarchists.
iMr. RALPH SMITH. You will find socialists in the House of Commons in England.

maintopic: SUPPLY-STATUTES OF THE PROVINCE OF SASKATCHEWAN.
speechtext: I am sure of one thing and that is that if my hon. friend were in the House of Commons in England, where his talents ought to bring him, he would not be sitting on the socialist side.

maintopic: SUPPLY-STATUTES OF THE PROVINCE OF SASKATCHEWAN.
speechtext: I would not exclude a man because he declared himself a socialist.

maintopic: SUPPLY-STATUTES OF THE PROVINCE OF SASKATCHEWAN.
speechtext: I never said I would either; but what I say is that the propaganda of the government has had the result of penetrating to the socialistic centres and bringing out the destitute to this country. If socialism means anything, it means an appeal to the destitute and the poor on the ground that they should have their share in the wealth of those who are rich.

maintopic: SUPPLY-STATUTES OF THE PROVINCE OF SASKATCHEWAN.
speechtext: Good doctrine.

maintopic: SUPPLY-STATUTES OF THE PROVINCE OF SASKATCHEWAN.
speechtext: But there is one doctrine superior to socialism, and my hon. friend has heard about it, I am sure, and that is the Christian doctrine. If you look into the report of the Department of the Interior-and here I crave your indulgence because I am going to start on dangerous ground, I am going to speak of the Belgian and French immigration. And I tell the minister of the Interior that I am going to raise all the racial appeal and appeals to prejudice that I raised last year, and will add another argument to which he may find an answer. If we look at the report of the Interior Department, we find that his immigration agents, the Church Army, were eager to bring to this country hooligans, scamps, ex-convicts, loafers and drunkards, but were not very eager to bring in Belgians or Frenchmen.

speakerposition: Minister of the Interior; Superintendent-General of Indian Affairs
maintopic: SUPPLY-STATUTES OF THE PROVINCE OF SASKATCHEWAN.
speechtext: Would the hon. gentleman define hooligans?

maintopic: SUPPLY-STATUTES OF THE PROVINCE OF SASKATCHEWAN.
speechtext:
Let the hon. minister look for the definition in his own department because it is his department that are bringing them out. As the old French proverb says:
Dis-moi qui tu hantes,
Je te dirai qui tu es.
Tell me whom you go with and I will tell you who you are.
Mr. OLIVER, Does the hon. gentleman say that the Department of the Interior directly or indirectly suggested the immigration of people such as he described?

maintopic: SUPPLY-STATUTES OF THE PROVINCE OF SASKATCHEWAN.
speechtext: Certainly, and I am going to prove it. Is the Church Army or is it not an immigration agent of the government.

speakerposition: Minister of the Interior; Superintendent-General of Indian Affairs
maintopic: SUPPLY-STATUTES OF THE PROVINCE OF SASKATCHEWAN.
speechtext: Certainly not.

maintopic: SUPPLY-STATUTES OF THE PROVINCE OF SASKATCHEWAN.
speechtext: My hon. friend has not looked into his own report, because he will find in it a whole page about the Church Army,

speakerposition: Minister of the Interior; Superintendent-General of Indian Affairs
maintopic: SUPPLY-STATUTES OF THE PROVINCE OF SASKATCHEWAN.
speechtext: That does not prove that the Church Army is an agent of the government or that the government is in any way responsible.

maintopic: SUPPLY-STATUTES OF THE PROVINCE OF SASKATCHEWAN.
speechtext: Is the Church Army not carrying on a propaganda ? Has it ever been disallowed by the government ? Is there a fine against such propaganda? Every police magistrate in England is an immigration agent for this country.

speakerposition: Minister of the Interior; Superintendent-General of Indian Affairs
maintopic: SUPPLY-STATUTES OF THE PROVINCE OF SASKATCHEWAN.
speechtext: I am not responsible.

maintopic: SUPPLY-STATUTES OF THE PROVINCE OF SASKATCHEWAN.
speechtext: Certainly, and in this way. The government has opened the door to that kind of immigration, and I am not quite sure that their agents have not said to the Salvation Army to send out more.' More than that, the Salvation Army is paid a special bonus by this government. Is that true or is it not.

speakerposition: Minister of the Interior; Superintendent-General of Indian Affairs
maintopic: SUPPLY-STATUTES OF THE PROVINCE OF SASKATCHEWAN.
speechtext: It is.

maintopic: SUPPLY-STATUTES OF THE PROVINCE OF SASKATCHEWAN.
speechtext:
Therefore there is no use in the hon. minister contradicting it. Take what Mr. Speers says, in the report of the Department of the Interior, about the Belgian immigration:
The great majority of the French and Belgian immigrants are farmers and have taken up land. Most of the Belgians and French Canadian immigrants and settlers have gone to Lake Monroe, Jack Fish, Moo-ejaw, Trampink lake, and southwest of Moosejaw >n Saskatchewan and in Manitoba some have gone east of Lake Manitoba, to Toulon and to Makinak. In Alberta these settlers have gone to the districts east of Stetler Daysland and on the Battle river, and a number have settled east and west of Red Deer and north of Morim-bille. Indications will show that possibly 150 families will be located north and east of Wood Mountain on the Canadian Pacific railway during this season.
And he says that these settlers are very successful and thrifty. And that, no doubt, is why we have just one immigration agent in Belgium. But there is more than that: when the famous North Atlantic Trading Company were in operation, when its members not known and were not in danger of being sent to prison or of being driven to suicide, why was it that this company did not operate in France or Belgium ? We were told then that the French government had the greatest objection to canvassing for emigrants and the French laws forbade it, and also that the Belgian government was very much opposed to canvassing for emigrants within that kingdom. We were told that, I think, by the minister himself.

speakerposition: Minister of the Interior; Superintendent-General of Indian Affairs
maintopic: SUPPLY-STATUTES OF THE PROVINCE OF SASKATCHEWAN.
speechtext: If the hon. gentleman will allow me, my memory is, that the reasons given were the direct opposite.

maintopic: SUPPLY-STATUTES OF THE PROVINCE OF SASKATCHEWAN.
speechtext: Oh, no, do

speakerposition: Minister of the Interior; Superintendent-General of Indian Affairs
maintopic: SUPPLY-STATUTES OF THE PROVINCE OF SASKATCHEWAN.
speechtext: Well, I have expressed the opinion and I may explain. The North

maintopic: SUPPLY-STATUTES OF THE PROVINCE OF SASKATCHEWAN.
speechtext: Atlantic Trading Company did not cover France and Belgium in its operations, because it was considered that in those countries it was possible to carry on an open propaganda for emigration, and so it was being carriecUon by a resident and duly accredited cotmtry agent in both countries. It was in other European countries that the North Atlantic Company operated because in those countries it was not possible to carry on an open propaganda.

maintopic: SUPPLY-STATUTES OF THE PROVINCE OF SASKATCHEWAN.
speechtext: I expected that answer from the Minister of the Interior, but he is caught there. Why is it that the North Atlantic Trading Company was operating in all the rest of continental Europe while there was no immigration agency or propaganda going on. in France or Belguim ?

speakerposition: Minister of the Interior; Superintendent-General of Indian Affairs
maintopic: SUPPLY-STATUTES OF THE PROVINCE OF SASKATCHEWAN.
speechtext: The only reason is that there was a propaganda going on in France and Belgium.

maintopic: SUPPLY-STATUTES OF THE PROVINCE OF SASKATCHEWAN.
speechtext: There was one man who used to be a professor of elocution in this country, M. Wialiard, and another man who was lame, M. Foursin Es-candre. That was the propaganda. And we were told by the minister-I remember it well-that the French government would not permit any more active propaganda, Well, perhaps he would say that as the propaganda went on, some men would be driven to suicide or would be sent to prison because the French laws would not permit an active propaganda.

speakerposition: Minister of the Interior; Superintendent-General of Indian Affairs
maintopic: SUPPLY-STATUTES OF THE PROVINCE OF SASKATCHEWAN.
speechtext: Does the hon. gentleman (Mr. Armand Lavergne) deny that the laws of France do not permit an active propaganda ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-STATUTES OF THE PROVINCE OF SASKATCHEWAN.
speechtext: I do deny it.

speakerposition: Minister of the Interior; Superintendent-General of Indian Affairs
maintopic: SUPPLY-STATUTES OF THE PROVINCE OF SASKATCHEWAN.
speechtext: Then I am afraid the hon. gentleman is not well acquainted with the laws of France.

maintopic: SUPPLY-STATUTES OF THE PROVINCE OF SASKATCHEWAN.
speechtext: I have the law of France here and I will read it.

maintopic: SUPPLY-STATUTES OF THE PROVINCE OF SASKATCHEWAN.
speechtext: From a newspaper.

maintopic: SUPPLY-STATUTES OF THE PROVINCE OF SASKATCHEWAN.
speechtext:
Yes. I do not believe in newspapers very much, perhaps, but I believe that this is a correct reprint of the law of France. Here is the title:
' Loi Francaise sur l'emigration.'

maintopic: SUPPLY-STATUTES OF THE PROVINCE OF SASKATCHEWAN.
speechtext: What date ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-STATUTES OF THE PROVINCE OF SASKATCHEWAN.
speechtext: '18 juillet, I860.' It has not been changed since.

maintopic: SUPPLY-STATUTES OF THE PROVINCE OF SASKATCHEWAN.
speechtext: What paper ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-STATUTES OF THE PROVINCE OF SASKATCHEWAN.
speechtext:
The best paper in Canada-' Le Nationaliste. Here is what the law says.
Article 1. Nul ne peut entreprendre les operations d'engagement on de transport des emigrants sans l'autorisation du ministre de

^agriculture, du commerce et des travaux publics.
That is the whole and sole prohibition in the French law of an emigration propaganda. I will translate it for the benefit of the Minister of the Interior.
No person shall undertake the operation of engaging or transporting emigrants without the authorization of the Minister of Agriculture, Commerce and Public Works.
And why is this ? It is explained in the rest of the statute-it is to safeguard the emigrants from suffering during transportation. And that is the whole and sole law in France prohibiting a propaganda in favour of emigration. I suppose the minister will be satisfied with this. Now, let us turn to the case of Belgium. In Belgium, not only does the government not prohibit canvassing for emigrants, but there is no emigration that the government of that country favours so much as emigration to Canada. Belgium is a very prosperous country. But it has too large a population for its superfices, and, as it has no colonies, it likes to send its surplus population to Canada. Thus, there was not only no prohibition. but there is actually encouragement in Belgium for emigration to Canada. But there was no active propaganda to encourage emigration. More than that, there was only one emigration agent, M. Treau de Coeli, who might do much better work if lie had better help. And. at the same time, this emigration, as shown by this very report of the Department of the Interior, is the best that can come to this country, as these people are farmers and succeed very well. And not only that, but, as I stated last year, when the Belgian exposition was held at Liege all the propaganda that was made for the older provinces amongst the Belgians in the form of pamphlets to encourage the Belgians to come to this country and these pamplets, by order of the commissioner of this government, were put in the cellar of the Canadian pavilion and ordered to be left there until the exposition should be over.

speakerposition: Minister of the Interior; Superintendent-General of Indian Affairs
maintopic: SUPPLY-STATUTES OF THE PROVINCE OF SASKATCHEWAN.
speechtext: Does the bon. gentleman (Mr. Arinand Lavergne) object to the payment of a bonus to Belgian booking agents?

maintopic: SUPPLY-STATUTES OF THE PROVINCE OF SASKATCHEWAN.
speechtext:
I object to paying a bonus to booking agents in any country. My position is clear, if the minister did not understand it last year. I hope he will understand it this year. He has put enough questions to ascertain it, but he may put as many as he likes and I shall be glad to answer them. I object to bonuses to booking agents in any country-France, Belgium, Germany, England, Scotland, Ireland or even the Russian countries that are the greatest friends of the Department of the Interior. As I have said before,-I cannot give it in the eloquent language of the hon.
minister, though it is practically the same idea-the result of the bonus system is quantity not quality and it tends to bring the undesirable instead of the desirable. This is the opinion that was expressed by the minister himself.

maintopic: SUPPLY-STATUTES OF THE PROVINCE OF SASKATCHEWAN.
speechtext: He was not minister then.

maintopic: SUPPLY-STATUTES OF THE PROVINCE OF SASKATCHEWAN.
speechtext:
I^o,-he
was a Little Canadian. We are told that the French do not emigrate-we have been told that many times. Certainly the French do not emigrate to this country as the British people do or as those of other continental countries do. But there is good reason for that. In France and Belgium the same propaganda is not carried on as is carried on in other countries. But I want to contradict the general statement. The French do emigrate. One proof is that there are 100,000 Frenchmen in the Argentine Republic. There are 50,000 French people in the United States.

maintopic: SUPPLY-STATUTES OF THE PROVINCE OF SASKATCHEWAN.
speechtext: What is the population of the United States ?

maintopic: SUPPLY-STATUTES OF THE PROVINCE OF SASKATCHEWAN.
speechtext: My recollection is that it is about 80,000.000.

maintopic: SUPPLY-STATUTES OF THE PROVINCE OF SASKATCHEWAN.
speechtext: The French immigration is not a large proportion.

maintopic: SUPPLY-STATUTES OF THE PROVINCE OF SASKATCHEWAN.
speechtext: Perhaps not, but it is enough to prove that the French do emigrate. If you look up the report of the Department of the Interior of France, for the year before last, you will find that 92,000 people left France in that year. I may be contradicted by some figures published in this country but the figures given by the French government are good enough evidence for me. I say that this bonusing of immigration can have two excuses-I will not say that it can have any justification. The excuse is either that the government wants to see the land speculators in the Northwest sell their lands or. as Mr. Smart, one of the government agents, said in Liverpool-and the Minister of the Interior cannot contradict me-to prevent this country from being Frenchified. The Minister of the Interior knows that Mr. Smart said that in Liverpool.

speakerposition: Minister of the Interior; Superintendent-General of Indian Affairs
maintopic: SUPPLY-STATUTES OF THE PROVINCE OF SASKATCHEWAN.
speechtext: I do not know that, he may have said it.

maintopic: SUPPLY-STATUTES OF THE PROVINCE OF SASKATCHEWAN.
speechtext:
I will read it to him again, I read it last year.
Tile ' Northern Express/ Liverpool,, February 10, 1902.-British blood is needed.

maintopic: SUPPLY-STATUTES OF THE PROVINCE OF SASKATCHEWAN.
speechtext:
Smart, Deputy Minister of the Interior of Canada, and Mr. W. T. R. Preston, immigration agent general for the Dominion, arrived in Liverpool to-day from London and Glasgow to arrange a gigantic system of British immigration to Canada.
Mr. Smart said this :
More British blood is also needed to be infused if the views of the Dominion of Canada



is not to be Frenchified by the rapid growth of the French population.
Is that the reason of the present immigration policy of this government, to prevent this country from being Frenchified ? I thought the spirit of this country was that we should cease talking about these questions. I am glad to take the same view that the member for Strathcona (Mr. McIntyre) did last year. I do not think I am raising any racial question, or any creed question, when I say that I see no reason why the deputy minister of this country should go to England and tell the people that they must prevent Canada from being Frenchified.

speakerposition: Minister of the Interior; Superintendent-General of Indian Affairs
maintopic: SUPPLY-STATUTES OF THE PROVINCE OF SASKATCHEWAN.
speechtext: I do not know that Mr. Smart said that.

maintopic: SUPPLY-STATUTES OF THE PROVINCE OF SASKATCHEWAN.
speechtext: I have just read what he said.

speakerposition: Minister of the Interior; Superintendent-General of Indian Affairs
maintopic: SUPPLY-STATUTES OF THE PROVINCE OF SASKATCHEWAN.
speechtext: I know what the hon. gentleman has read, but I do not believe that Mr. Smart ever said it.

maintopic: SUPPLY-STATUTES OF THE PROVINCE OF SASKATCHEWAN.
speechtext: Well, I believe that Mr. Smart did say it, not only do I believe it, but I am sure of it. I read it last year, and I asked the Minister of the Interior to contradict it. If he could have contradicted it he would have done so, but he has not contradicted it. The Minister of the Interior knows that the province of Quebec counts for something in the majority of this House, and that these words of Mr. Smart will not help the government in the next election ; therefore he would have contradicted these words if he could. Mr. Smart has not contradicted them, and he cannot contradict them. The minister said that the best immigration we could have into this country was not people from foreign countries, but our own Canadians, and that the best immigration policy was to prevent Canadians going to the United States, and send them to the Northwest. But what do we see ? We see that it costs less to bring an immigrant from the continent of Europe to the Northwest, than it does to take a man from the province of Quebec to the Northwest. This cannot be contradicted. If the government wants an immigration policy, why dont they adopt the policy of sending people from the older provinces to settle in the Northwest ? That is not what is being done, that is not what this government is encouraging, but that is what this government is opposing.

maintopic: SUPPLY-STATUTES OF THE PROVINCE OF SASKATCHEWAN.
speechtext: I understood the hon. gentleman to say, or to intimate, a short time ago that too many foreigners were being infused into the population of Montreal and the province of Quebec. Now he puts forward the idea that the government is making no effort whatever to settle the older provinces.

maintopic: SUPPLY-STATUTES OF THE PROVINCE OF SASKATCHEWAN.
speechtext:
I did not say that, I said that the bonus system of Mr. A. LAVERGNE.
immigration adopted by this government 'had the result of bringing to this country, not farm labourers, but men who are criminals in their own country, according to the declaration of the Italian consul in Montreal, men who come to this country under false pretenses, and who are swarming into our cities because they do not know how to work. If you abandon the bonus system you will improve the quality of immigrants a hundred per cent, because they will not be attracted to this country by the false representations of booking agents, but by the contented settlers who have preceded them in this country. The new comers will settle in the older provinces instead of going to the Northwest. I have asked this government why it was that under the present system, a young man of the older provinces had to pay more for a transportation ticket to go to the Northwest than the foreign born European or the citizen of the British Isles. That is what I complain of.

maintopic: SUPPLY-STATUTES OF THE PROVINCE OF SASKATCHEWAN.
speechtext: I would like to ask the hon. gentleman if he thinks it should form any part of our immigration policy to move population from one part of Canada to the other.

maintopic: SUPPLY-STATUTES OF THE PROVINCE OF SASKATCHEWAN.
speechtext:
I do think so, because that is the way that western Canada lias been settled. If the hon. gentleman will study the history of our country lie will see that the people of the old provinces have been gradually spreading out west, and the settlers that go from eastern Canada are no worse than those who come from foreign countries ; I think they are much better, because they are Canadians. That is my policy ; but the policy of this government seems to be to bring in masses of people without regard to quality, to fill up the western country and help speculators sell their lands in the west. They are trying to get every kind of immigration except French speaking immigration. Every right is denied to the French speaking element except the right of paying. But the Douk-hobors can run around naked from place to place. Sir, I think the policy of this government will lead to the political murder of our country. As has been well said by many economists, we are laying the foundation for a mongrel nation in Canada. According to the report of the Department of the Interior itself, we are laying the foundations of a mongrel nation. I say that is political murder, and I say that from a French Canadian point of view it is not only political murder but it is suicide. as it has been well pointed out by one of the greatest economists in the world, Mr. Louis Arnould, in 'La Revue des Deux Mondes.' Some hon. members of this House may have no objection to committing suicide, but I have, and I will never be an ac-

above the imports. I think, as a matter of fact, they are a little below-far below. The prosperity they' bring is that of crime, disease and idiocy. Therefore, if this is all the prosperity that these immigrants bring in to our country we have no need for prosperity of that kind, and the minister ought to remember that prosperity does not mean the bringing about of a greater amount of criminality or an increase in the number of lunatics in our country. If we compare our prosperity with that of the United States we must come to the conclusion that the United States has to-day the worst immigration problem of any country in the world to face. To-day they have a restrictive policy. They have to face the whole question and it will be remembered that one president of the United States has been assassinated by anarchists. If that is the future prosperity that immigrants are going to bring to our country, we may well expect in the very near future that the Canadian-born population will be at the mercy of the foreign-born population and will become an insignificant minority. Therefore, for these considerations, if I have to take a stand against my political party on this question, it is because I place above party the future of my country and if, on this question as on many others, I have to choose between my party and the future happiness of my country, I choose my country.
On motion ot Mr. Verville, the debate was adjourned.
Sir WILFRID LAURIER moved the adjournment of the House.

maintopic: SUPPLY-STATUTES OF THE PROVINCE OF SASKATCHEWAN.
speechtext: Does this debate go on to-morrow?

speakerposition: Prime Minister; President of the Privy Council
maintopic: SUPPLY-STATUTES OF THE PROVINCE OF SASKATCHEWAN.
speechtext: This debate will go on.
Motion agreed to, and House adjourned at 11.50 p.m.
Tuesday, April 14, 1908.
